title: A.I. Hurricane Models Were Front and Center as Isaias Headed Toward Land
source_used: Moneycontrol (relaying CNN of 8 Oct 2026); WDSU for context
key_facts: The US National Hurricane Center put significant weight on Google DeepMind's AI model when forecasting Hurricane Isaias.
Per CNN, conventional models disagreed on strength and path; the AI guidance supported a forecast that Isaias would become a Category 2 hurricane when the first advisory was issued on Tuesday.
NHC director Michael Brennan said DeepMind performed well last season and showed greater consistency between successive forecasts.
NHC predicted Hurricane Melissa in 2025 could reach Category 5 while still Category 1, drawing on DeepMind's projections.
Forecasters use AI and traditional models together; AI predictions must be checked against satellite and other observations.
As Isaias approached the northeastern Gulf Coast, the wider consensus among forecasting systems also pointed to a likely hurricane landfall.
WDSU (8 Oct): the NHC leaned toward AI models including Google AI, while most physics-based models leaned further west.
quote_evidence: The US National Hurricane Center placed significant weight on Google DeepMind’s artificial intelligence model when forecasting Hurricane Isaias, choosing to follow its projections more closely than several traditional weather models.
That meant the threat was not based on AI projections alone.

Yet artificial intelligence predictions cannot be relied upon blindly; their accuracy is dependent on the quality of training data, and their predictions have to be validated against satellite information, air data, and weather prediction systems.
why_it_matters_hint: Forecasters are using an AI model's early warnings of strong storms, alongside traditional models.
